summary:
Re-verified against the current tree (grind pass, 2026-08-04): the tree had moved substantially since this map was last written — an intervening owner-review-1 pass had already built the search modal, the +new session/workspace dialog, and the workspace-files wiring that this map still called 'missing'/'not-wired'. This pass re-measured every non-match item against the live prototype markup (design/prototype/Clio Session.html, not guesswork), fixed the remaining real gaps, and corrected the map. Fixed this pass: the topbar's cyan hover now carries the measured background+border tint (was color-only) and the icon-only observability eye correctly gets no background tint (border+color only, per the prototype's own style-hover); the rail's New(+) button now hovers cyan/bordered, distinct from Search's neutral hover (previously identical); the search trigger's accessible name now reads the prototype's full title text; the search modal's header is now the prototype's single icon+input+close row instead of an extra 'search' title bar the app had invented; search's workspace rows now navigate (open that workspace's files) instead of being a dead no-op on click AND on Enter; the rail's 'open in files' workspace-menu action had a real bug — it shared one piece of state with the +new dialog's own workspace pre-selection, so opening files for workspace B could silently show workspace A (whichever session happened to be active) instead; fixed by giving each affordance its own state, with a regression test locking the CLICKED workspace wins. The 'agents' footer cell now carries a title describing what it actually does (connection switching) rather than promising nothing; Settings already has its own Agents page, so the prototype's 'opens settings' contract has a real path alongside the connection-switch click. Genuinely unresolved this pass: the hierarchy ribbon is still hardcoded to 'main' — populating it needs Call()-block click wiring in the transcript surface (HandoffPart.tsx, outside this surface's file boundary) plus a focus-stack navigation model the app does not have yet; it duplicates work already tracked as a separate task (E9, 'new Call-agent grammar') and was not built here to avoid a shallow, half-wired duplicate of that effort. The 'relay' footer cell remains a deliberate, documented degrade pending clio-agent#1179 (no reachability endpoint exists).

PASS 2 (2026-08-05): re-verified every non-'match' item against the current tree — no other pass had touched this surface since PASS 1 (b17e3acc). The independent audit (8c0267c6) had already corrected two statuses here: the 'agents N' footer cell match->deviates (its click opens a connection switcher, not the prototype's plain Settings navigation — cross-checked against menus-grammar.json, which records the SAME control as 'deviates' for the SAME reason and, in its own PASS 2, re-confirmed the divergence as a deliberate, documented non-fix: rewriting the click to only navigate would delete a working, tested multi-backend feature the prototype's single-connection demo never modelled). That click-semantics divergence stands unchanged here too — but re-measuring the CONTROL beneath it (not just its click target) against the prototype's raw markup turned up a real, previously unflagged bug: the dot's COLOR was wrong. The prototype's agents/relay footer dots are a plain static `background:var(--t-ok)` (green), never a state machine — the app had been driving the agents dot through the session-lifecycle `running`/`idle` vocabulary, where `running` renders the busy/in-progress accent (orange) by this app's own design-system convention, not green. A real, healthy connection (readyCount>0) was rendering the WRONG color independent of prototype-matching. Fixed by adding a proper static 'ok' state to the shared StatusDot vocabulary (kept honestly conditional — idle/grey when readyCount is 0, never a false-positive green). Sweeping the same class of gap (hover states) across the whole rail found six more: the workspace group row, session row, and all three footer cells had been hovering on the generic `--t-hv` token where the prototype's own style-hover attributes measure `--t-sf2` verbatim on every one of them (`--t-hv` never appears anywhere in the prototype's rail markup at all); the per-row '...' menu buttons (session and workspace) and 'show more' had picked up a background-on-hover the prototype never gives them (color-only there, same grammar as the topbar's icon-only eye); the topbar's blueprint-crumb hover was missing its cyan color change entirely (background-only, on the wrong token); and the session TITLE had no hover cue at all for its click-to-rename affordance (the prototype fades in a var(--t-sf2) fill on hover; the app showed nothing). All fixed, all re-verified by a live Playwright hover capture measuring computed background/color/border against the prototype side by side (every value now byte-identical). Also added the prototype's collapsed-rail brand mark (a small logo/glyph next to 'Show sessions') and that control's own always-visible border + darker hover border, both previously absent. The relay cell and hierarchy ribbon are unchanged and re-confirmed accurate: relay remains the deliberate visible-degrade pending clio-agent#1179 (no reachability endpoint), and the ribbon remains hardcoded to 'main', still correctly deferred to E9 (cross-surface: needs Call()-block click wiring in HandoffPart.tsx plus a focus-stack view-swap model, neither of which exist yet).

Both files now agree, as required.
items.app_evidence: Click semantics: content divergence remains deliberate (apps/web/src/shell/Rail.tsx:482-492 comment): the app manages MULTIPLE live clio deployments the prototype's single-backend demo never modelled, so the click opens a connection switcher rather than only navigating — but the prototype's own 'opens settings' contract is still honoured, since Settings has its own Agents page (apps/web/src/settings/Settings.tsx case 'agents') listing the same connections. Honesty fix (real title text) landed a prior pass: `title="Connected agents — click to switch the connected backend"` (Rail.tsx). Count itself is live (GET-driven readyCount). PASS 2 (2026-08-05): re-measuring the CONTROL beneath the click (not just its target) against the prototype's raw markup (`background:var(--t-ok,#34d399)`, no state binding at all — a plain static green, never a state machine) found a real, previously unflagged bug: the dot was driven through the session-lifecycle `running`/`idle` vocabulary, where `running` renders this app's own busy/in-progress accent (orange), not green — wrong even independent of prototype-matching. Fixed: added a static 'ok' state to the shared StatusDot vocabulary (apps/web/src/kit/StatusDot.tsx, apps/web/src/kit/statusdot.css) and switched the agents cell to it when readyCount>0, keeping 'idle' (grey) when nothing is ready — never a false-positive green (apps/web/src/shell/Rail.tsx:509-516). Live Playwright hover/rest capture against the prototype: dot color now byte-identical (rgb(52,211,153) both sides), as is the cell's own hover background/color. Regression-locked: apps/web/tests/unit/rail-and-topbar-grind.test.tsx ('renders "ok" ... when at least one connection is ready' / 'falls back to "idle" ... when nothing is ready').

items.element: Hierarchy ribbon (row directly under the topbar)
items.proto_truth: data-driven breadcrumb of the currently-focused agent hierarchy (`{{ ribbon }}` sc-for): starts at 'main', gains a hop for each child agent the user has navigated into (e.g. 'main › geospatial'), the active/live hop shows a small orange pulsing dot (animation:clio-pulse), each hop is clickable and jumps back to that depth (`go: () => this.setFocus(focus.slice(0, i+1))`)
items.app_evidence: Re-verified, unchanged — still a real gap, NOT built this pass. apps/web/src/session/SessionView.tsx (`ribbon={[{ id: 'main', label: 'main' }]}` — still hardcoded); apps/web/src/shell/AppShell.tsx:130-138 (the ribbon RENDERING primitive is ready — it's a plain Tabs list driven entirely by the `ribbon` prop, so it already supports N hops and correct active/inactive coloring); apps/web/src/transcript/parts/HandoffPart.tsx (the Call()/child-card block) has zero navigation affordance — no onClick, no callback prop — confirmed via grep across apps/web/src/transcript for any 'scope'/'onFocusChild' reference: none exist anywhere in transcript rendering. WHY NOT FIXED HERE: populating this needs (1) a click handler on Call() blocks in HandoffPart.tsx — outside this surface's file boundary (transcript-parts, not rail-and-topbar) — and (2) a focus-stack navigation model this app does not have at all (the prototype's version doesn't just highlight a ribbon hop, it SWAPS THE ENTIRE TRANSCRIPT to show the child agent's own view — a materially bigger feature than a breadcrumb). This exact work is already tracked as a separate, in-progress task ('E9 implementation — new Call-agent grammar'); building a shallow version here (a ribbon hop with no corresponding transcript swap behind it) would be a half-wired duplicate of that effort, not a fix. PASS 2 (2026-08-05): re-grepped HandoffPart.tsx and SessionView.tsx/AppShell.tsx — no change since PASS 1; still correctly deferred to E9.
items.backend_surface: the session/turn data needed (child session ids, live status) is reachable via the same GET /v1/sessions/{id} + turn data the transcript itself renders from — not a missing endpoint, a cross-surface client feature
items.fix_hint: WIRE GAP — carried forward as E9, not fixed here. Populate `ribbon` from a child-agent focus stack (push a hop when a Call(...) block is followed, pop on back-navigation), give the active/live hop the orange clio-pulse dot, and — the larger piece — build the corresponding view-swap so entering a hop actually shows that child's own transcript, matching the prototype's `setFocus`/`viewVals` model rather than just relabeling the current one.
